films.title: Foragers
films.description: Foragers depicts the dramas around the practice of foraging for wild edible plants in Palestine with wry humor and a meditative pace. Shot in the Golan Heights, the Galilee and Jerusalem, it employs fiction, documentary and archival footage to portray the impact of Israeli nature protection laws on these customs. The restrictions prohibit the collection of the artichoke-like ’akkoub and za’atar (thyme), and have resulted in fines and trials for hundreds caught collecting these native plants. For Palestinians, these laws constitute an ecological veil for legislation that further disposses them from their land while the Occupation’s representatives insist on their scientific expertise and duty to protect. Following the plants from the wild to the kitchen, from the chases between the foragers and the nature patrol, to courtroom defenses, Foragers captures the joy and knowledge embodied in these traditions alongside their resilience to the prohibitive law. By reframing the terms and constraints of preservation, the film raises questions around the politics of extinction, namely who determines what is made extinct and what gets to live on.

films.title: Four by Jean Vigo
films.description:
Veronica Project Space is pleased to present the complete filmography of the inimitable Jean Vigo.

In his brief 29 years, Vigo established a cinema of poetic realism fusing humanistic stories with surreal sequences that ooze of craft. While divisive in his time, Vigo’s work gained a resurgence of interest through posthumous praise from critics, including his daughter Luce, that deeply influenced the French New Wave movement.

The four films in this presentation (a mix of documentary and narrative) are warm and surprisingly innovative offerings to the art of cinema that remain timelessly impactful to audiences and filmmakers nearly a century onward.

Friday, November 13, 2026, 7pm

165 min.

Free admission for this program.

Images, films, and individual synopses provided by Janus Films.

films.title: Gioia
films.description: Gioia is a french literature teacher who has never known love, except for the suffocating kind from her parents, with whom she still lives. Among the students at her school is Alessio, who uses his body as a means to earn money and help his mother, a cashier in a supermarket. A forbidden, fragile, and inexplicably necessary bond grows between Alessio and Gioia. But Alessio's desire for social and personal redemption becomes a silent poison that keeps him from fully surrendering to Gioia's disarming sweetness. And so, he destroys everything and erases the only person who has ever loved him.

films.title: Go Fish
films.description: Max (co-writer Guinevere Turner) a young, lesbian, college student living in Chicago is in aromantic dry spell. Her roommate Kia (T. Wendy McMillan), sets Max up with Ely (V.S. Brodie), an older woman that Max initially dismisses but ultimately falls for, until it’s revealed that Ely may already be committed.

films.title: God Forgives Everyone
films.description: Thirty-five-year-old Palermo real estate agent Arturo lives a carefree life, with no lasting relationships and a passion for classic Sicilian pastries. His routine is disrupted when he meets Flora, the charming and determined daughter of a renowned local pastry shop owner and a fervent Catholic. To win her over, Arturo agrees to play Jesus in a Via Crucis procession, despite knowing almost nothing about religion. When Flora discovers the truth, Arturo makes an unusual commitment: for three weeks, he will follow the teachings of the Gospel to the letter, turning faith into action, with an unexpected spiritual mentor guiding him along the way: the Pope.

films.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
films.description:
War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life.

Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant.

There is no third time. Everything ends here.

films.title: Her Song
films.description: Olivia, a Franco-American writer, returns to her ancestral village in the south of France to write the story of her grandmother, who fled Paris during the Nazi invasion during World War II. There, she meets Madeline, a talented local artist, who quickly replaces her grandmother as the face of the novel. As a number of strange coincidences ensue, fiction and reality intermingle uncannily, and Olivia starts to ask whether she's part of history's unfolding story, or vice-versa.

films.title: Hocus Pocus
films.description: In this bewitching story, three mischievous witches are inadvertently resurrected when teenager Max Dennison discovers an ancient spellbook in Salem. Along with his sister Dani and new friend Allison, Max must stop the witches from carrying out a nefarious plan. The trio of witches, portrayed by Bette Midler, Sarah Jessica Parker, and Kathy Najimy, wreak havoc as the children race to steal their spellbook and prevent a wicked curse from engulfing the town

films.title: Idle Hands
films.description:
Anton is a teenage burnout whose daily agenda consists of smoking weed, watching TV and accomplishing absolutely nothing. Then his right hand gets possessed by the devil and murders his parents. Soon his two best friends are dead, Anton is trying to cut off his own arm, and the hottest girl in the neighborhood is somehow still interested in him. Luckily, death doesn’t prevent anybody from hanging out.

IDLE HANDS could only have escaped from 1999: Devon Sawa in enormous pants, Seth Green and Elden Henson as undead couch potatoes, Jessica Alba in angel wings, The Offspring playing the school Halloween dance and Rob Zombie’s “Dragula” on MTV while everybody gets high on the couch. It captures teenage life in the last few minutes before everything went digital—a suburban wasteland of weed, music videos, convenience stores and endless hours with absolutely nothing to do. Then it dumps a homicidal severed hand into the middle of it and starts spraying glorious rubber gore. Some of it has aged badly, some of it has aged beautifully, and somehow this deeply stupid movie has only grown more lovable with time.

films.title: Journey to Italy
films.description: Married for eight years with no children, Brits Katherine and Alex Joyce are driving to Italy, their ultimate destination just outside of Naples to sell the villa they have just inherited from his uncle, the villa where they will be staying during their time there. On the drive, they come to the realization that this trip marks the first time that they have truly been alone together, and as such don't really know one another in the true sense. While in Italy, they end up mainly embarking on pursuits separate from each other - Katherine preferring the cultural, Alex preferring "company" including with some acquaintances they didn't know were in Naples until running into them on their first night in the city - and on the few occasions when they do spend time together, there is a tension and an underlying increasing want on both sides to hurt the other emotionally in their individual beliefs of what the other is thinking or has done in their time apart. As their marriage slowly falls apart, the question becomes if there is any way to salvage it if they truly do want to continue to be Mr. and Mrs. Joyce.

films.title: Kokomo City
films.description:
In the wildly entertaining and refreshingly unfiltered documentary Kokomo City, filmmaker D. Smith passes the mic to four Black transgender sex workers in Atlanta and New York City – Daniella Carter, Koko Da Doll, Liyah Mitchell, and Dominique Silver – who unapologetically break down the walls of their profession. Holding nothing back, the film vibrates with energy, sex, challenge, and hard-earned wisdom.

This vital portrait, edited and shot by Smith in bold black and white, is her feature directorial debut. A two-time Grammy-nominated producer, singer, and songwriter, Smith made history as the first trans woman cast on a primetime unscripted TV show. Executive produced by Lena Waithe, KOKOMO CITY won the Sundance Film Festival’s NEXT Innovator Award and NEXT Audience Award, as well as the Berlinale’s Audience Award in the Panorama Documentary section.

films.title: Kwaidan
films.description: This visually and aurally ravishing widescreen film, perhaps the greatest of Masaki Kobayashi, is adapted from the ghostly tales of Lafcadio Hearn, the Greek-Irish writer who made Japan his home in the 1890s. The level of stylization – in color, composition, music, sound, speech and movement – of these four tales is never less than breathtaking. Kwaidan bankrupted Kobayashi’s production company, but the effort was well worth it: there’s nothing else like it in all of cinema. Made in close collaboration with the great composer Toru Takemitsu.

films.title: Land of the Dead: it's for the gays
films.description: Presented by Scorpio Rising Productions. Land of the Dead: it’s for the gays is a dark, campy horror comedy that explores the intersections of gender identity, addiction, trauma, and Queerness. Through Mel’s confrontation with a literal demon from their past, the film examines the ways unresolved pain can shape identity, relationships, and self-acceptance. Blending supernatural horror with Queer humor and emotional depth, the story uses camp as a tool for both survival and reclamation, creating a space where confronting the past becomes a path toward healing and embracing one’s authentic self.

films.title: Late Autumn
films.description: The great actress and Ozu regular Setsuko Hara plays a mother gently trying to persuade her daughter to marry in this glowing portrait of family love and conflict—a reworking of Ozu's 1949 masterpiece Late Spring.

films.title: Love Fits Everything
films.description: Stefano Rovelli is the author of a small book called "How to Leave Your Partner in 7 Steps and Be Happy." Federica is a young woman currently on a break with the partner. She thinks it's Federico's fault, since he loved Rovelli's books, and won't back down until she and her ex are back together. Frank is a singer paired with a young rapper who only uses autotune. Manlio, Frank's manager, is called to the Vatican, and has to reunite Frank and his ex-partner, Milly, to sing for the Holy Father. Too bad Frank and Milly hate each other and have no plan to ever sing together again. Vittoria Casati is a unpopular politician. To boost her consensus, she decides to host a refugee from Africa. When she is faced with a Ghanan man instead of a boy, she welcomes him into her home, alongside her husband Giovanni and their two children.

films.title: Love Streams
films.description: Robert is in headlong flight from the stifling love of the lonely women he writes about in his novels. His sister, Sarah, has alienated their family with precisely that sort of stultifying love. As the streams of their lives, loves and dreams intertwine, these two lost souls begin to find each other and ultimately, themselves.

films.title: Mad Monster Party?
films.description:
By 1967, the monsters had made it. Dracula, Frankenstein, the Wolf Man and the rest of the old horror gang had escaped the graveyard and taken over television, toy stores, model kits, comic books and the bedrooms of monster-crazed kids everywhere. There was really only one thing left to do: throw a party.

And what a party. Rankin/Bass took the stop-motion wizardry behind RUDOLPH THE RED-NOSED REINDEER, handed the monsters over to MAD Magazine legends Harvey Kurtzman and Jack Davis, brought in Boris Karloff to preside over the festivities and Phyllis Diller to play Frankenstein’s extremely talkative mate, then invited every creature they could squeeze onto the Isle of Evil. Dracula! The Wolf Man! The Mummy! Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde! The Invisible Man! Zombies! Skeletons! A Peter Lorre-looking ghoul! Jack Davis designed them, a studio full of Japanese animators built them, and somebody had to move every single one of these maniacs one frame at a time.

The result is a glorious 1960s monster-kid fever dream where Frankenstein discovers a formula capable of destroying all matter and celebrates by announcing his retirement. There are musical numbers, terrible puns, monster politics, a skeleton rock band called Little Tibia and the Fibias, Dracula dancing and enough lovingly handcrafted gothic clutter to fill a dozen Halloween specials. Part monster rally, part MAD Magazine cartoon brought to life and part Rankin/Bass holiday special for the greatest holiday of them all, MAD MONSTER PARTY? is what happens when an entire generation stops being afraid of monsters and starts letting them babysit their kids.

films.title: Making Marie Antoinette
films.description:
Eleanor Coppola's behind-the-scenes documentation of her daughter Sofia directing the 2006 film MARIE ANTOINETTE, capturing the craftsmanship and challenges of being a young female director.

Polarizing upon its release, Sofia Coppola’s MARIE ANTOINETTE is now, 20 years later, widely embraced as a 21st-century cinematic cornerstone and a distilled expression of its director’s recurring themes of celebrity, wealth, and isolation. For the first time, Coppola’s dynamic craftsmanship in creating her personal vision for the brief life of the 18th-century queen in the years leading up to the French Revolution is on full display in this diary shot by her mother, filmmaker Eleanor Coppola, on the film’s set in Versailles in 2005.

From almost 80 hours of video, Eleanor began to assemble the footage during the pandemic lockdown, and Sofia helped finish editing it after Eleanor’s death in 2024. Narrated by Diane Lane, reciting Eleanor’s journals from the time, this is a rare behind-the-scenes glimpse that is both process-oriented and touchingly personal.

films.title: Man of Marble
films.description: In the 1970s, student filmmaker Agnieszka investigates the life of a 1950s bricklayer and discredited labor hero who is only remembered through statue representations in cellars and storage lockers. Discovering facts about the bricklayer have been suppressed, she has to decide whether to pursue the truth or not while navigating the complexities of communism's rise in Poland. Mixing satirical humor and poetic storytelling, this thought-provoking examination of the moral responsibility of an individual and the way art can challenge dominant ideology remains one of Wajda’s most unique productions.

films.title: Marie Antoinette
films.description:
20th anniversary screening of Sofia Coppola's pastel-soaked cult classic, newly restored in 4K.

Coppola brings a candy-colored palette, a dreamy synth-pop soundtrack, and Converse high-tops to eighteenth-century Versailles for this exuberantly subversive, extravagantly stylized anti-biopic of one of history’s most infamous (and perhaps misunderstood) figures.

Kirsten Dunst portrays Marie Antoinette as a rebellious teenage princess, who marries the awkward young dauphin of France (Jason Schwartzman), soon to be crowned King Louis XVI. Feeling isolated in a royal court rife with scandal and intrigue, Marie Antoinette defies both royalty and commoner by living like a rock star—which can work for only so long.

Named the 10th best movie of the 21st century by The Big Picture podcast.

films.title: Matchstick Productions
films.description:
Matchstick Productions returns with their 34th annual ski film, The Way Out, a raw

tribute to the timeless culture and lifestyle of skiing. Dropping you straight into heavy

Alaskan spine lines, deep Japanese powder, and iconic Swiss villages. This film shows

skiing as far more than a sport; it’s a path toward total freedom. From legendary

veterans to rising breakout talent, the message is simple: the soul of skiing isn’t dead; it's waiting wherever snow falls.

films.title: Members Only Mystery Movie - November 2026
films.description: Have you ever wanted to get a sneak preview of some of The Forum’s upcoming programming at an exclusive, members-only event? This is your chance to do just that! Join us for our November 2026 installment of our Members Only Mystery Screenings, where we can promise you you’ll be treated to an evening with a fantastic film, but you’ll only know what it is right before you see it!

films.title: Met Opera 2026/2027: Carmen
films.description: Richard Eyre’s beloved production of Bizet’s masterpiece returns to theaters, led by mezzo-soprano Elīna Garanča as the title character and tenor Roberto Alagna as Don José in the indelible 2010 Met performance—a fan favorite of The Met: Live in HD series. Yannick Nézet-Séguin conducts in his company-debut season.

films.title: Mrs. Miniver
films.description:
A moving drama about a middle-class English family learning to cope with war, told in a series of dramatic vignettes. The family, headed by the lovely and gracious matriarch, endures the departure of the father for the beaches at Dunkirk, the discovery of a wounded Nazi pilot, the death of the daughter-in-law in an air raid, and the entry of the son into the Royal Air Force.

Every movie starts with a story at the North Bend Theatre. Just prior to each of the Love & War movies, our resident film experts, Kevin & Beth, will share the amazing stories behind these great films, giving you a whole new way to connect to the movie.

films.title: My Brother's Wedding
films.description:
In this tragicomic work of realism, Pierce Mundy (Everett Silas) is employed at his parents’ South Central dry cleaners with no prospects for the future — his childhood buddies are all in prison or dead. Pierce’s best friend Soldier (Ronnie Bell) is just getting out of jail. Pierce’s brother Wendell (Monte Easter), an up-and-coming lawyer, is busy planning a wedding to a snooty upper-middle-class black woman named Sonia (Burnett’s wife, Gaye Shannon-Burnett, who co-produced the film). Pierce’s pious, Bible-touting mother (Jessie Holmes) provides occasional comic relief but also a heartfelt moral backbone to the film, as she urges Pierce to accept his responsibility to his family.

When Soldier is killed in a car accident, Pierce’s conflicting obligations to family and friends becomes manifested in the choice between his brother’s wedding and his best friend’s funeral— both falling on the same day. The film’s climax has Pierce desperately trying to be two places at once and ending up nowhere.

“The story focuses on a young man who hasn’t made much of his life as of yet, and at a crucial point in his life, he is unable to make the proper decision, a sober decision, a moral decision. This is a consequence of his not having developed beyond the embryonic stage, socially. He has a distinct romantic notion about life in the ghetto and yet, in spite of his naive sensitivity, he is given the task of being his brother’s keeper; he feels rather than sees, and as a consequence his capacity for judging things off in the distance is limited. This brings about circumstances that weave themselves into a set of complexities which Pierce desperately tries to avoid.”

— Charles Burnett

films.title: My Neighbor Totoro
films.description:
The 4pm shows are dubbed in English.
The 7pm shows are in the original Japanese with English subtitles.

Hayao Miyazaki's celebrated family favorite reminds us to appreciate nature and our bond with the world around us.

After moving with their father to be closer to their hospitalized mother, Satsuki and Mei soon discover the friendly spirits of the nearby forest, who help the girls deal with their feelings in a difficult time.
Co-starring Catbus.

films.title: My Night at Maud's
films.description: I exist. What is my essence? What do I choose? Éric Rohmer, one of the founding New Wave figures, liked to stroll the streets of Paris. Even if he had a planned destination, he was open to the music of chance. Rohmer’s characters are solidly self-directed, but they can be surprised by life. In a provincial town, Jean Louis (Jean-Louis Trintignant) believes he’ll meet his dream woman and marry her, and he spots college student Françoise (Marie-Christine Barrault) in church. He’s determined that she will be the one, but he hasn’t even met her. Unplanned things happen: Jean-Louis runs into his old friend Vidal (Antoine Vitez), who suggests that they visit his friend Maud (Françoise Fabian), one of the most liberated New Wave heroines, who has broken many traditional barriers (she’s an accomplished physician, highly cultured, and a loving single parent). The three stay up late, drinking and discussing freedom of choice. Vidal leaves, it’s snowing heavily, why not have Jean-Louis stay the night? There’s one bed; Maud sleeps naked. Rohmer’s cinema explores forward motion and hesitation, the nature of things, and cosmic grace. New Wave women show the way.

films.title: Nationtime
films.description:
Nearly ten thousand Black Americans converge on a high-school gymnasium in Gary, Indiana, with the extraordinary ambition of deciding their future together. Republicans share the room with revolutionaries. Agreement is hardly guaranteed. Invited by Amiri Baraka to document the National Black Political Convention, William Greaves captures the exhilaration—and combustible difficulty—of turning a gathering into a political force.

The director of SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM has an exceptional feel for what happens between people, and NATIONTIME finds its drama in the current running from the podium to the bleachers and back. Jesse Jackson works the room into a thunderous call-and-response; Baraka struggles to hold it together when delegates object. The stakes extend well beyond the gym: a national agenda demanding guaranteed income and health care, a struggle over who gets to speak for whom. Then Richard Roundtree walks onstage and barely needs to speak at all. With Isaac Hayes supplying the soul, this extraordinary film brings the sheer physical excitement of collective possibility roaring onto the screen.

films.title: Natural Born Killers
films.description: Oliver Stone's NATURAL BORN KILLERS is an all-out assault on the American appetite for violence, made with the manic enthusiasm of a man who appears to share it. Woody Harrelson and Juliette Lewis are Mickey and Mallory Knox, a pair of homicidal lovers whose cross-country killing spree turns them into national celebrities, aided by a television industry that has finally discovered the perfect marriage of entertainment and mass murder. Stone attacks the material with an almost psychotic barrage of film stocks, animation, rear projection, sitcom laugh tracks, and hallucinatory editing, creating a movie that seems to be having a nervous breakdown in front of your eyes. Released at the height of the O.J. Simpson era, NATURAL BORN KILLERS was condemned as an irresponsible glorification of violence by people who apparently hadn't noticed what the rest of American television was broadcasting. Thirty years later, its vision of a country where murder is content, notoriety is currency, and the public can't get enough of either feels considerably less exaggerated than it once did.

films.title: Next of Kin
films.description:
When Linda inherits her mother’s sprawling retirement home in rural Australia, she returns to a place she hasn’t seen since childhood and discovers that the elderly residents have started dying with suspicious regularity. Then she finds her mother’s old diaries, which describe eerily similar deaths decades earlier. There are figures at windows, faucets that won’t stop running, footsteps in empty rooms and an enormous old house that seems determined to keep Linda from ever getting a decent night’s sleep.

NEXT OF KIN spends its first hour moving at the speed of a nightmare you can’t quite wake up from, then suddenly remembers it’s an Australian horror movie and all hell breaks loose. Director Tony Williams smothers the film in rain, shadows, long hallways and creeping dread, while Tangerine Dream veteran Klaus Schulze’s pulsing electronic score keeps the dread humming. Together they turn a retirement home into one of the great haunted spaces of ’80s horror without ever settling comfortably into a ghost story. Elegant, eccentric and quietly menacing, NEXT OF KIN keeps tightening the screws until its stately Gothic nightmare finally cracks open and something much wilder comes spilling out.

films.title: Night of the Vamp-Friars
films.description:
The first feature film wholly produced by Vinegar Syndrome Pictures; directed by Kurtis M. Spieler (Re-Director of New York Ninja).

A group of friends in a punk rock band discover a hidden cemetery in the woods, where they accidentally raise a horde of undead friars.

Shot entirely on 16mm film, Night of the Vamp-Friars is a loving tribute to the homegrown horror films made during the height of the video store era.

Presented with The Grand Illusion.

films.title: Nosferatu
films.description:
The Halloween tradition is back!

Danny Kolke will be accompanying the classic silent film, Nosferatu (1922), with his wonderfully spooky organ soundtrack!

films.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
films.description:
One afternoon in August 1972, at the behest of legendary, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves, a coterie of luminaries from the Harlem Renaissance gathered—with cameras rolling—for an intimate party in Duke Ellington’s townhouse. Fifty years later, completed by Greaves’ son David, ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM has emerged as a rapturous living archive of one of the most important artistic movements of the 20th century and, posthumously, one of the most important works in the Greaves filmography.

A towering constellation of artists, poets, painters, musicians, scholars, and other notables appear throughout — among them Aaron Douglas, Arna Bontemps, Richard Bruce Nugent, James Van Der Zee, and Countee Cullen’s widow, Ida Mae Cullen. Free from any institutionalized gaze and structure, they congregate around a large punch bowl to drink, reminisce, banter, and passionately debate their legacy. The conversations we’re privy to flow naturally and candidly, marked variously by humour, fervour, reflexive insight, and not a bit of melancholy, as they take stock of their achievements in their older age.

Greaves’ multiple 16mm cameras are at the heart of the action, capturing and partaking in the collegial repartee, while the deft, contemporary editing balances the original ’70s textures with an exhilarating, contemporary immediacy, tracing the urgency of these artists and their ideas from the 1920s through to the 1970s and to our present moment.

Functioning as well as a dynamic inquiry into the ways culture is actively inherited and sustained across disciplines, and creates communities of protest and survival, ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM is a monumental reclamation of cinematic and cultural memory.

films.title: Once Upon a Time In Seattle
films.description:
A perpetually living project, Once Upon a Time in Seattle returns to Northwest Film Forum in a revised, expanded (and shorter!?) edit for this special encore engagement. Comprised of moments from 50 films shot in Seattle (up from 47 in the previous iteration,) and a few irresistible facsimiles, Once Upon a Time in Seattle is part love letter, part loony action adventure, and part free-associative meditation on the transience of landscape in a city that has always had a complicated relationship with honoring its past while moving swiftly (recklessly?) into the future.

There is no linear narrative, and dialogue is kept to a minimum. The city itself is both location and protagonist, while the function of the human characters, or perhaps more accurately, ciphers, is that of a vessel to move us through the city and occasionally offer loose context or comic relief.

No single existing shot or sequence is sustained longer than a minute, with most individual shots lasting less than 20 seconds, and over half clocking in at 5 seconds or less. The result is a deceptively complex amalgamation of wholly unrelated material, and an impressively unique editorial/directorial achievement.

Surprisingly weaving numerous throughlines from the many disparate existing narratives, while leaving much open to the viewer’s interpretation, scene chronology floats between seemingly non sequitur, to quietly poignant, depending on the viewer’s own history with the city.

A hyper-local, one-of-a-kind film experience and an opportunity to examine Seattle’s ever-changing landscape as seen through the camera lens, Once Upon a Time in Seattle offers a unique portal to examine our city’s topography (and vibe!) of the past, both near and distant.

If you saw the premiere in September and loved it, come see how it’s changed!

films.title: Open Arthouse: Meet the Staff!
films.description:
It's been a while! The last few years, there have been a lot of changes at the Forum, most notably the makeup of our staff!

To kick off our new series of events, Open Arthouse, we invite you to come by the Forum from 5:30-7:30 to mix, mingle, and meet the staff. Get to know the people who are keeping the lights on and making sure you're given some of the best films the city has to offer, and meet your other fellow film lovers!

Attendance is free, drinks will be at happy hour prices all night, and maybe we have another event to announce in-person ;)

films.title: Perdita Durango
films.description:
Somewhere beyond David Lynch's WILD AT HEART lies PERDITA DURANGO, Álex de la Iglesia's spectacularly disreputable take on the American mythology of lovers on the run. Here, romantic devotion is measured in the trail of bodies left behind. Adapted from a novel by Barry Gifford, whose characters also inhabit Lynch's film, this deranged collision of outlaw romance, black comedy, and occult horror ventures into territory few filmmakers would dare approach. Even at its most appalling, the film maintains an exuberance that makes it difficult to know whether to laugh or recoil.

Rosie Perez plays Perdita, a ferocious outlaw who finds her soulmate in Romeo Dolorosa (Javier Bardem), a grinning criminal and self-styled sorcerer with a taste for human sacrifice. Together they embark on a cross-border crime spree involving two kidnapped American teenagers and a series of grotesque rituals. Perez and Bardem are sensational together, bringing an almost indecent amount of sexual energy to their shared appetite for destruction. Their performances give the film its reckless momentum, while the collision of Mexican folk religion and American pop culture lends the proceedings a particularly bizarre flavor. Long butchered for American distribution, PERDITA DURANGO also features James Gandolfini as a federal agent investigating the smuggling of a truckload of human fetuses, a detail that should give you some idea of what you're getting into.

films.title: Pierrot le Fou
films.description: A poet experiences the world and expresses it in words, images, emotions. Pierrot is Jean-Luc Godard’s free-form ode to “an artist and his girl in love, the last romantic couple,” made poignant because his seven-film relationship with Anna Karina, and their marriage, would soon be over. In the film they are personified as Ferdinand (Jean-Paul Belmondo) and Marianne (Anna Karina). Ferdinand, fed up with his life of oppressive bourgeois conformity, leaves his marriage-with-child for spontaneous road adventures with babysitter Marianne. In a euphoric rule-breaking rush, the couple speeds to an idyllic secluded island on the French Riviera. Ferdinand is now free to contemplate quietly and work on his book, with Marianne as his affectionate, inspiring companion. But she loves to sing and dance: “I’ve had it with nature, eating from cans, that’s it!” So its back to “civilization,” and what Marianne calls “a police novel, revolvers, nightclubs.” Ferdinand discovers that there’s more to Marianne’s story than he realized, and he responds accordingly, moment-to-moment: existential choice made profoundly literal. As Godard says, “The world between two flickers of the eyelids, the sadness between two heart-beats.” When Karina boldly gazes into Godard’s camera, at us, we feel both their hearts beating. In Godard’s deeply personal cinema, love can be both lost and eternal, the horizon where sun unites with sea.

films.title: Powwow People
films.description:
As an immersive, observational story, Powwow People invites audiences to witness the unfolding of a powwow over the course of a single day. Emcee Reuben Little Head is the perfect guide, grounded, generous, and often hilarious. The film's final 30-minute long take is deeply inclusive, creating space for viewers to simply be present with community. It's a powerful reminder that to witness in this way is a privilege and a blessing.

—Tracy Rector

“the audience is the real winner for the privilege of having shared the company of so many talented people, the rich textures and engaging sonic environment of a powerful summer day’s gathering” – Josh Bis, The SunBreak
films.director: Sky Hopinka (Ho-Chunk Nation/Pechanga Band of Luiseño Indians)

films.title: Pretty Poison
films.description:
There's something deeply wrong with the American girl next door, and Noel Black's PRETTY POISON is delighted to investigate. A spectacularly twisted combination of teenage romance, black comedy, and small-town psychosis, this neglected cult classic stars Anthony Perkins and Tuesday Weld as two young lovers whose shared enthusiasm for make-believe takes them into increasingly unpleasant territory. Perkins plays a recently institutionalized fantasist who convinces a beautiful high school majorette (Weld) that he's a secret agent investigating a Communist conspiracy. She proves an enthusiastic recruit, although her ideas about what constitutes an appropriate response to enemy activity turn out to be considerably more extreme than his.

Coming a few years after Psycho, PRETTY POISON finds Perkins playing another socially maladjusted young man with serious psychological problems, only this time he may be the most reasonable person in the movie. Weld is astonishing as a wholesome American teenager whose cheerful disposition remains entirely undisturbed by the increasingly appalling things she's willing to do. Black directs with a wonderfully straight face, but it's the warped chemistry between Perkins and Weld that makes the film irresistible. He's thrilled to have found someone who believes his fantasies; she's thrilled to have found someone who gives her an excuse to act on hers.

“If PSYCHO was the seed of a new kind of mainstream Hollywood movie ... then this is the brightly colored fruit.” - Joe Gibson

films.title: Puerto Rican Short Film Night
films.description:
A Fundraiser for the Diaspora of the Puerto Rican Independence Party.

Join us for a night of film, art, and Puerto Rican pastries with the DIASPORA OF THE PUERTO RICAN INDEPENDENCE PARTY and LA ANTILLANA. We will be showcasing three short films that highlight the effects of colonialism in different manifestations throughout Puerto Rico’s history and remind us why we fight for the independence of Puerto Rico.

MATARON A PEDRO (2026, Kristian Mercado)

In 1930s Puerto Rico, Pedro Albizu Campos and his wife Laura Meneses navigate the island-wide sugar cane workers' strike, the brutal machinery of colonial repression, and the fierce, sustaining love between two people who refused to surrender their dignity or their dream of freedom.

MELAO (2024, Val Vega)

Nando, a desperate worker on a sugarcane plantation in 1950s Puerto Rico who struggles to care for his pregnant wife, until he fixes on a plan that he hopes will secure their future and lead them out of poverty, no matter how crazy it may seem.

MAREAS A LA DERIVA (2026, Camila Sofía Rodríguez López)

Maite, a young graffiti writer in Puerto Rico, faces a life-altering choice: leave the island for a promising career opportunity abroad or stay and navigate the challenges of a nation in crisis. During her mother’s birthday weekend, with her sister visiting from New York, Maite sees two possible futures reflected in them, one rooted in resilience and staying, the other shaped by the opportunities of leaving. Grappling with these paths, she is forced to reckon with a paradise built for tourists and outsiders to enjoy but for locals to labor in and endure, shaped by systemic neglect, colonialism, and a broken power grid that keeps its bliss just out of reach for its own people.
films.director: Kristian Mercado, Val Vega, Camila Sofía Rodríguez López

films.title: Romanian Film Festival Seattle: 3 Days in September
films.description: Bianca’s world shatters when her fiancé’s mistress crashes their wedding. Reeling from shock, she flees on a tourist train, launching a real-time odyssey of chaotic escape and surreal encounters through the off-season seaside resort. Rejecting her old life, she transforms her humiliation into a liberating night of rebellion, ultimately embracing a new path as the sun rises.

films.title: Romanian Film Festival Seattle: Atlas of the Universe
films.description: Ten-year-old Filip travels with his father to the nearest town to buy new shoes for school. When his father gets side-tracked by an old friend, Filip is left to continue the journey alone. A simple mistake at the shoe shop—buying two right-foot shoes—sets him on an unexpected adventure through an unfamiliar world. Too ashamed to return home empty-handed, Filip decides to fix the problem himself. Along the way, he befriends a stray dog, names him after his favorite football player, and finds an unlikely companion. Through small choices, moments of fear, and quiet courage, Filip takes his first steps toward independence and growing-up.

films.title: Romanian Film Festival Seattle: Blindsight
films.description:
Laura suffers from severe amnesia and depression following an accident, so she can’t
remember who the people around her are. She is reluctantly persuaded by her family to go
on a boat trip to Türkiye, but the closer she gets to her destination, the more unclear the
reality and the purpose of the trip becomes. They are caught up in a series of situations in
which they change their minds depending on the context, their own principles are called into question.

films.title: Romanian Film Festival Seattle: Kontinental '25
films.description: When Orsolya oversees the eviction of a local elderly man in Cluj, Transylvania, the unintended consequences come to shatter her and her understanding of her place in society. Spiraling into an existential crisis, she traverses the city, meeting with various people in her life — her husband, an old friend, a former student, a priest — to consider and reconcile her place in an increasingly maddening modern world in this furious and hysterical, moral parable.

films.title: Romanian Film Festival Seattle: R.M.N.
films.description: A few days before Christmas, having quit his job in Germany, Matthias returns to his multi-ethnic Transylvanian village. He wishes to involve himself more in the education of his son, Rudi, left for too long in the care of his mother, Ana, and to rid the boy of the unresolved fears that have taken hold of him. He’s preoccupied with his old father, Otto, and also eager to see his ex-lover, Csilla. When a few new workers are hired at the small factory that Csilla manages, the peace of the community is disturbed, underlying fears grip the adults, and frustrations, conflicts and passions erupt through the thin veneer of apparent understanding and calm.

films.title: Romanian Film Festival Seattle: The Last Transhumance
films.description: Some 10,000 years ago, in the Middle East, man first domesticated sheep, and took them “on the road.” That's what shepherds call transhumance. Their journey measures time and space with tools we have forgotten. People and herds swing between plains and mountains, setting in motion a mechanism that has ticked for thousands of years yet is about to stand still. The transhumance clock stops each time a family of shepherds choose to no longer take to the road. Nevertheless, it keeps ticking through the stubbornness of those who continue to sleep among their sheep under the clear sky – the remaining few who still live under the stars. The Last Transhumance film is their story.

films.title: Romanian Film Festival Seattle: The Wall
films.description: In a village where everyone knows everything and nothing is forgiven, two families with a truly comical history find themselves at loggerheads over a piece of land. Both are convinced the truth is on their side, and things spiral completely out of control just as wedding bells should be ringing. Between unyielding boundaries, inflamed egos, and utterly eccentric relatives, a happy ending to the marriage seems increasingly unlikely.

films.title: Romanian Film Festival Seattle: The Yellow Tie
films.description: The epic true story of Sergiu Celibidache, following the legendary composer from a childhood spent under his father’s draconian authority, through to adulthood as he masters his craft in Berlin. However, his greatest struggle emerges at the outbreak of war. With the world collapsing around him, Sergiu must evade death and starvation to cement his place in the world of classical music, as he risks being torn apart by a relentless pursuit for perfection that could overshadow his legacy forever.

films.title: Romanian Film Festival Seattle: Traffic
films.description: Natalia and Ginel leave their small Romanian Danube village to work abroad in a big Flemish city. One evening, when she is assaulted after meeting a local, Natalia asks Ita, a friend from home turned into a crook, to help her. Ita uses their frustration against the values of a world they consider to be arrogant, decadent, and historically guilty for their misery as second-rate citizens – invisible migrants. The result is a tragi-comical, ideological heist only revealing the complete lack of communication between East and West, between rich and poor, between masters and slaves.

films.title: Route One/USA
films.description:
“A thin stretch of asphalt cutting through all the old dreams of a nation.”

Renegade filmmaker of the New Left Robert Kramer (Ice, Milestones) returned to the US in 1988 following nearly a decade of living abroad. In an effort to grasp the realities his former country faces, Kramer documents his travels down the entirety of Route 1, from Fort Kent, Maine to Key West, Florida (America’s “end of the rainbow”), accompanied by his buddy Doc, a physician back from a distressing decade in Africa. Throughout, Doc searches for steady work while interviewing veterans, refugees, teachers, activists, and presidential candidates, with such pit stops along the way as a Native American reservation in Maine, foodbanks, Walden Pond, and evangelical churches that preach the “truth” about Disney. Except there’s a catch: Doc is not, in fact, a doctor, but a fictional character played by actor Paul McIsaac. The slippery nature of reality and fiction blur in this monumental portrait of ‘80s America, a wholly unique moviegoing experience shot in stunning Super 16mm.

This screening will include a 15 minute intermission.

films.title: Salvation
films.description:
“A provocative allegorical powder keg.”– David Rooney, The Hollywood Reporter

In a remote village in eastern Turkey, a village has been divided in two by a decades-old land feud. The Hazerans inhabit the upper village; the Bezaris lived in the lower village, before being driven into exile. Upon their return, a rumor arises that the Bezaris intend to steal the Hazerans' land. While the Hazerans' leader, Sheikh Ferit, advocates for calm, compromise, and coexistence, his troubled brother, Mesut, takes a different approach.

Beset by nightmares that he interprets as visions, Mesut convinces the Hazerans that salvation for one side can only be achieved through the eradication of the other. The people respond with enthusiasm, fueled by a sense of grievance and righteous indignation, and keen to see themselves as principled defenders of their own land, rather than the usurpers of their neighbors'.

While the story of the film is based on actual events, director Emin Alper blurs dream sequences and reality and combines realism with a highly stylized aesthetic to conjure a timeless tale with no shortage of resonance today.

Winner of the Silver Bear Grand Jury Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.

films.title: Seattle Film Society Presents Locals Only: October 2026
films.description:
October is for terror! On tap this month are flesh eating nightmares and unexplained disappearances, unnerving polaroids and weekends gone wrong. Not to mention a freak you won’t be able to unsee. For all the horror-heads out there, this one’s for you:

- POLAROID by Joey Greene: A young man is thrust into a terrifying mystery when the Polaroid photos that he has taken reveal something that isn’t actually there. (3 Min)

- BEST FRIEND MATERIAL by Mel McCarthy & Nathan Blanchard: A guys weekend goes wrong. (15 min)

- ADHESION by Mark Woo: A vain party clown suffocates in her own flesh-eating nightmare. (4 min)

- MOTHER OF NIGHT by Mohamed Abdullahi & Rayana Mohamed: After a series of unexplained disappearances, a night-shift waitress investigates a ghostly local myth and discovers the horror may be terrifyingly real. (13 Min)

- LOOK AT THIS FREAK by Alex Furnas: A reunion of old friends is disrupted by a hated roommate and something else that’s even worse. (15 Min)

This event is presented in partnership with the Northwest Film Forum. Join us for a screening and Q&A with drinks to follow at Linda’s Tavern! See ya at the movies!

films.title: Seattle Turkish Film Festival: Dump of Untitled Pieces
films.description:
Ambitious photographer Asli candidly takes photos of people’s hands to reveal the stories they may tell. Her best friend, computer savvy Murat cooks simple dishes full of love, but sometimes with already spoiling vegetables. They live together nearly like a married couple, who never sleeps together. Barely able to afford anything, they are treated as nothing and face eviction due to unpaid bills. 20 months ago rebellious Asli took up a camera to reclaim her broken heart. She wears a mask of confidence to pursue the luxury of being an artist in the pretentious art world. Asli dreams of showcasing her photos and escaping uncertainty, despair and loneliness with the hapless introverted Murat as her manager.

Filmmaker Melik Kuru comes from an editing background, including his editing work for SIFF 2024 official selection Hesitation Wound.

films.title: Seattle Turkish Film Festival: Sevda
films.description: Tülin Özen, from SIFF 2024 favorite Hesitation Wound (2023), stars as Sevda, a real estate developer in Istanbul, is about to complete the project of her career. But construction hits an obstacle: the elderly caretaker of an Ottoman cemetery refuses to leave his home among the graves. This face-off stirs up buried memories. Then a call from Elif, a Turkish immigrant in Switzerland, upsets her: the father who abandoned her is dying and asking to see her. The call reveals an unsuspected link between her family's past and the city's transformation. Sevda premiered at the Zurich Film Festival.

films.title: Seattle Turkish Film Festival: Those Who Whistle After Dark
films.description: Mr Melih, the retiring manager of the Natural History Museum, clumsily tries to adapt to civilian life. After a supernatural encounter, his innocent middle age depression spirals into a major existential crisis. He seeks solace from his family, but they are busy with their own crises. His wife Suzan, an ambitious nurse that is stuck in a life she's disappointed with, has fallen victim to a scam she cannot tell to anyone. In the meantime, their video-game addict daughter Toprak, a young unemployed aspiring writer, plots a doomed escape to the U.S. to run away from the increasingly bleak future in Turkey. With Melih searching for the meaning of his life, Suzan secretly trying to find a way out, and Toprak going nowhere fast; soon they are all haunted by the ghosts of the past - literally.

films.title: Seattle Turkish Film Festival: Yellow Letters Gala Film + Party
films.description:
Winner of several awards including the Golden Bear (Berlin International Film Festival), Yellow Letters is directed by İlker Çatak, who previously won accolades for his film The Teacher's Lounge (2023). Derya and Aziz, a celebrated artist couple from Ankara, lead a fulfilling life with their 13-year-old daughter Ezgi – until an incident at the premiere of their new play changes everything. Overnight, they find themselves targeted by the state and lose their jobs and their home. They move to Istanbul to temporarily stay with Aziz’s mother. While Aziz ekes out a living with odd jobs and holds on to his convictions, Derya searches for a way to become financially independent. An increasing distance grows between them and their daughter until they are forced to choose between their values and their shared future as a family. The film stars Özgü Namal (from Turkish TV series such as Ezel, Merhamet, Kizil Goncalar), and former STFF guest Tansu Biçer (from STFF 2024 gala film Dormitory, and Netflix series Midnight At The Pera Palace).

This is the Gala Film + Party Event. Gala film at SIFF Uptown, followed by Party at KEXP.
Please note: Not included in STFF Full Series Pass.

films.title: SECS Fest 2026
films.description:
FULL SCHEDULE AND TICKETS ARE AVAILABLE AT:

https://secsfest.org/secs-fest-2026-festival-schedule/

SECS FEST is a sex-positive international film festival celebrating the artistry of erotic cinema while inspiring diverse communities to engage in adult conversations about sex.

THE FESTIVAL

SECS Fest is held in November at the Beacon Cinema, Seattle. Once involved with providing a small selection of short films as part of the Seattle Erotic Art Festival, SECS Fest became an independent, non-profit film festival in 2016, to better serve filmmakers and fans of erotic film. Due to theater closures in Seattle, WA due to the COVID-19 pandemic, SECS Fest 2020 was a virtual festival, hosted by PinkLabel.tv. SECS Fest has returned as an annual, in-person, film festival.

The festival will include films that reflect the diversity of human sexuality and thus, a broad range of sexual practices and orientations will be on display. We will curate a selection of short films (to be presented in 90 minute programs) and feature length films (60 -120 minutes). The films may be narrative fiction, experimental, animation, and even documentary and will include a broad range of genre (drama, comedy, romance). And the programming will include works from all over the globe. Special attention will be given to films that defy audience expectations for sexually explicit films, that some believe are inherently sexist and hetero-centric, so festival programming will attempt to include films from female and non-binary creators and films that depict underrepresented populations, and thus will challenge heteronormativity, ableism, racism, sexism, etc.

Additionally, SECS Fest will include archival programs to explore the long history of sex in the cinema. SECS Fest programmers will curate archival programs included in the festival.

SECS FEST 2026 will mark 10 years of SECS FEST.

films.title: Shaolin Soccer
films.description:
25th anniversary screening of Stephen Chow's wildly entertaining martial arts sports action comedy!

Hong Kong screen legend Stephen Chow directs and co-stars in this high-octane, cult-favorite genre mashup, in which a down-and-out footballer joins forces with an idealistic kung fu master in hopes of leading their ragtag team of Shaolin monks to victory on the pitch.

The full, uncut, original Hong Kong version, presented in Cantonese with English subtitles.

Special live intro from local Hong Kong genre film connoisseur and one of the programmers of the Seattle Film Society, Patrick McFarland.

films.title: Short Film Nominee Showcase
films.description: Each year, the Seattle Film Critics Society (SFCS) honors Pacific Northwest filmmaking as part of their annual awards. A selection committee carefully considered dozens of short films released this year whose primary production took place in the Pacific Northwest and selected five as initial nominees for this year’s Best Pacific Northwest Short Film award.

films.title: Spookies
films.description:
“A surreal blitz of ooze, slime, hoboes, failed birthday parties, Grim Reapers, explosions, zombies, people jumping through walls, and a guy with his own face silkscreened on his shirt.” — Joseph A. Ziemba, BLEEDING SKULL!

After taking shelter in a spooky old mansion, a group of travelers discover a ouija board and decide to spend the night. But they soon learn that playing with the forces of black magic isn't fun and games, and it's not long before they're battling demonic creatures, shape shifters, and other forms of evil! Of all of the bizarre horror films made in the 1980s, SPOOKIES easily ranks among the weirdest. The film became a fan favorite thanks to its expertly rendered creature effects and notorious for its bizarre production history in which its original creators were fired and replaced by Eugenie Joseph, who added new scenes and re-edited the previously shot footage. Newly restored in 4K from its long lost original negative, SPOOKIES has never looked better.

After discovering her passion for cinema in a small building called the Film Center at her university, a student decides to explore the memories of the place and the people who once shared the same passion.

Emrah, who works as a receptionist in the night shift of a boutique hotel, is constantly monitored by his boss Adem through security cameras and this surveillance becomes increasingly irritating.

After finding out that her soon-to-be-ex-husband will be stopping by to pick up his belongings, ER nurse Songul decides to go home late. To pass the time, she starts helping an elderly man search for his missing granddaughter.
