A man finds himself alone in an eerie hotel, at the center of a dark plan. Everything in the hotel seems to operate according to a rule he does not know

films.title: Street Fighter
films.description: In 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu and Ken Masters are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don't, it's GAME OVER!

films.title: Surplus Operations and Instruments: Experiments in Cinéma Vérité and Psychodrama
films.description:
IN THE COMPANY OF MEN and EMERGENCY WARD respectively exemplify the seemingly opposed tactics that Greaves used to extract truth from reality: psychodramatic performance and cinéma vérité. Psychodrama was a tool that Greaves used in his acting classes but which was originally developed for therapeutic use and involves breaking societal roles through deep subconscious digging in group therapy skits. Cinema verite is nearly the direct opposite and requires non-direction to allow reality to play out as it would but in front of a camera.

The notion that brings them together is spontaneity, which for Grieves was the explosion of truth that occurs at the peak of both forms. A performance when it reaches a state of therapeutic internal awareness or when the camera happens to catch a nurse when she has a few moments to share about the stress she goes through at her work. In these two short films we see Greave’s laying the groundwork for his long-term ambitions to make documentaries that spoke to the needs and interests of the Black community and to push acting through artifice and back into the real.

IN THE COMPANY OF MEN (1969)

Produced by Newsweek, IN THE COMPANY OF MEN offers profound insight into how psychodramatic role-playing and sensitivity training can generate constructive dialogue between white supervisors and Black employees. Concerned with increasing numbers of the “hardcore unemployed” during the late 1960s, companies began hiring consultants to foster honest conversations that uncovered mass resentment among workers toward their managers’ overt and covert racism. In an echo of his SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM experiments, William Greaves calls upon raw, guerrilla-style camera work to observe how African American men use these sessions to express long-suppressed anger in the face of consistent professional humiliation. Among the outcomes is their bosses’ dawning recognition of the brutal realities that encourage so many skilled laborers to suffer unemployment rather than endure the demeaning American workplace.

EMERGENCY WARD (1959)

Made in 1958, Greaves's first NFB effort EMERGENCY WARD is a fascinating work that reflects the transition in documentary from didacticism to Direct Cinema and its director’s clear glee at finally having a full toolbox. A half-hour portrait of the emergency ward at Montreal General Hospital, the film is driven by several tensions: between a calm narrator who reassures us of the staff’s “expert knowledge” and Greaves's urgent, off-camera voice asking them blunt questions about “mistakes”; between static shots of dull routine and handheld shots of frantic chaos; and between the faith in institutions urged by the film and the suffering and loneliness it depicts. Beautifully shot by Wolf Koenig and kinetically edited by Greaves, the film is an explosion of technique that boasts several unforgettable images and announces Greaves's arrival as a filmmaker – he even appears on camera at one point, leaning against a window while listening to an orderly’s rambling anecdotes. Nevertheless, one gets the sense that Greaves is itching for a freer form or more expansive subject, honing his craft while waiting to make the films he wanted to make. (Brian Belovarac)

films.title: Sweetheart - Opening Night Film + Party
films.description: Ten-year-old Nico is forced to spend the summer in Sicily with his elderly Aunt Gela, a woman deeply rooted in the traditions of her homeland and unfamiliar with the digital world. Accustomed to social media, online chats, and modern life, Nico struggles to adapt to his aunt's lifestyle, and their relationship begins with tension. Yet, as they share everyday moments and navigate their differences, an unexpected and genuine bond emerges. Gela learns to see the world through her nephew's eyes, while Nico discovers the value of friendship, family, and traditions from a disappearing era. Their lives will never be the same.

films.title: Symbiopsycho-Taxiplasm: Take One
films.description:
In his one-of-a-kind fiction/documentary hybrid SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE, the pioneering William Greaves presides over a beleaguered film crew in New York’s Central Park, leaving them to try to figure out what kind of movie they’re making. A couple enacts a breakup scenario over and over, a documentary crew films a crew filming the crew, locals wander casually into the frame: the project defies easy description. Yet this wildly innovative sixties counterculture landmark remains one of the most tightly focused and insightful movies ever made about making movies.

“What if they made a revolution and nobody saw it? That’s what happened in 1968, when William Greaves filmed one of the most daring and original movies of the time… It’s one of the greatest movies about filmmaking ever made, and one that would have spoken to young independent filmmakers of the time. It’s a vision of filmmaking that didn’t get seen when it could have made a decisive difference for a new generation… The movie is no mere self-exploration or self-reflection but a vision of the times, a crucial work of late-sixties politics in action.” - Richard Brody, The New Yorker

films.title: Take Me Home
films.description:
Anna, a 38-year-old Korean adoptee with a cognitive disability, cares for her aging parents in a fragile balance of meeting each others’ needs. When a Florida heat wave shatters their family and Anna’s routine, her future is uncertain - until she creates a world where she can thrive.

Join us for a post-film Q&A on Saturday, October 24th at 5:30PM with Sibling Support Project and The Arc of Washington State. Panelists include: Rep. Jamila Taylor; Stacy Dym, Executive Director of The Arc of Washington State; Emily Holl, Director of Sibling Support Project; and Writer/director Liz Sargent (via Zoom).

films.title: Tampopo
films.description:
The tale of an enigmatic ramen ronin who guides the widow of a noodle shop owner in her quest for the perfect recipe. Tampopo serves up a savory broth of culinary adventure, seasoned with offbeat comedy and the erotic exploits of a gastronome gangster.

Sweet, sexy, surreal, and mouthwatering, Tampopo remains one of the most delevtable examples of food on film. It's been remastered in 4K, making this an extra delicious big screen treat.

films.title: Taste of Cherry
films.description:
The austere, middle aged Mr. Baadi drives around the dusty hills on the outskirts of Tehran with a somber goal: searching for someone who will bury him after he commits suicide, a taboo under Islamic law. As he winds his way through the warm, autumnal landscape, Baadi picks up various passengers (a soldier, a seminarian, and a taxidermist) to engage in reflexive conversations on mortality and individual choice. Despite the grimness of its end of the road subject matter and the weight of the decision with which Baadi grapples, Taste of Cherry remains a life affirming and euphoric film experience. Along with being the first Iranian film to win the Palme d’Or, it subsequently brought Abbas Kiarostami’s masterful body of work to full international prominence.

“Kiarostami, one of the great filmmakers of our time, is a master at filming landscapes and constructing parablelike narratives whose missing pieces solicit the viewer’s active imagination.” — Jonathan Rosenbaum, Chicago Reader

films.title: Tenzing
films.description: Based on true events, “Tenzing” chronicles the little-known story of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok), a gifted Himalayan climber who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston), became the first to summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing finds an ally in expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe). Together, they persuade Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) that Tenzing belongs on the British climbing team, rather than merely serving it. Where Western climbers see “Everest” as something to be conquered, Tenzing reveres “Chomolungma” as the sacred mother goddess. What follows is an ascent defined as much by the tensions between backgrounds, classes and competing ambitions as by the perils of the mountain itself. But high above the world, empire, rank and aspiration fall away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — and for Tenzing, the fulfillment of both a lifelong dream and a spiritual calling. Directed by award-winning filmmaker Jennifer Peedom, “Tenzing” is a story of greatness that refuses to be diminished — and the love that makes it possible.

films.title: The Backcourt Documentary - Basketball's Best Kept Secret
films.description: Based on the Amazon bestselling book "The Backcourt," The Backcourt Documentary chronicles the remarkable story of Tucson basketball legends Delano Price and Hoegie Simmons, the best-kept secret of Southwest playground folklore. Their friendship and dynamic backcourt helped lead Tucson High School to the 1969 state championship, but their story extends far beyond basketball. Through personal interviews, history, and reflection, the film explores brotherhood, triumph, adversity, and the social forces that shaped their lives and generations around them, including the Great Migration, the crack epidemic, the explosion of gang culture and its amplification through 1990s media narratives, and the prison-industrial complex. At its heart, The Backcourt is a story about two gifted men whose lives took dramatically different paths while their shared legacy endured.

films.title: The Birch Wood
films.description: Young Stanislaw, riddled with tuberculosis, departs Switzerland to spend his final days with his introverted forester brother Boleshaw on their secluded farm. This return home reignites a sensual passion for life, music, and love, giving him a vibrant energy at odds with his mournful brother. Their conflicting emotions lead to confronting repressed guilt and reconciliation of the past. Set in the early 1930s, this intimate character study offered Wajda the opportunity to explore areas outside of his intensely political war films and contemplate nature through reworking motifs from classic Polish landscape and symbolist paintings in this elegant depiction of early twentieth century provincial life.

films.title: The Burning of Moses Seattle
films.description:
Seattle bears the name of a Duwamish leader, but the United States government still refuses to recognize the Duwamish Tribe. Two new documentaries by Seattle filmmakers examine the enduring consequences of dispossession and the unfinished struggle for justice in the city built on Duwamish land.

David Norman Lewis's THE BURNING OF MOSES SEATTLE investigates the mysterious, unsolved murder of Chief Seattle's grandson, uncovering a disturbing chapter of local history where mythology, family memory and historical mystery intersect.

In UNRECOGNIZED: THE DUWAMISH TRIBE, director BJ Bullert examines the tribe's decades-long fight for federal recognition, a battle involving contested historical records, political opposition, and the extraordinary situation of a people forced to prove their continued existence in their own ancestral homeland. Through interviews and archival materials, Bullert reveals how the consequences of Seattle's founding remain very much alive in the present.

“UNRECOGNIZED is a compassionate and unfiltered examination of the impact the Pacific NW's colonial era continues to have on native lives today — especially the people of the Duwamish Tribe, now deemed "extinct" despite their ongoing and visible presence in the Northwest's largest city. The story of the Duwamish and their struggle for recognition is essential history — not just for Seattle, but for the nation and the many indigenous people whose existence we deny to this day.” - BJ Cummings, author, The River that Made Seattle: A Human and Natural History of the Duwamish

films.title: The Devils
films.description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption –and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is the uncut and unfiltered theatrical experience that Russell always envisioned – and the first time the film will be presented restored and in 4K.

films.title: The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie
films.description: Luis Buñuel orchestrates consistent unpredictability through narrative pivots and tonal shifts in his satirical masterpiece that won France an Oscar for International Feature Film and received a nomination for Original Screenplay, co-written by Jean-Claude Carrière. A series of happenings sewn together amid a relatively consistent motif is driven by the six French bourgeois who persistently pursue a dinner plan that is repeatedly interrupted by random incidents. In this repetitive digression, the value of the earnest pursuit becomes trivial, exposing the absurdity of the characters’ thoughtless actions. — Academy Museum of Motion Pictures

films.title: The Girl Can't Help It
films.description:
In 1956, rock and roll was threatening to destroy American civilization, and Jayne Mansfield was threatening to destroy the structural integrity of the buildings around her. Naturally, Frank Tashlin decided to put them both in the same movie. Mansfield plays Jerri Jordan, a spectacularly proportioned blonde whose gangster boyfriend (Edmond O’Brien) is determined to make her a singing sensation, despite the minor complication that she may not actually be able to sing. Enter a washed-up talent agent (Tom Ewell), who discovers that behind Jerri’s world-famous figure is a sweet, ordinary girl whose greatest ambition is to stay home and cook dinner. Unfortunately, the rest of America has other plans for her.

A former Looney Tunes animator with a genius for turning the human body into a public safety hazard, Tashlin unleashes a CinemaScope carnival of exploding milk bottles, melting ice, screaming teenagers, colors that practically glow in the dark. Between the gags comes an astonishing parade of rock and roll royalty, including Little Richard, Fats Domino, Gene Vincent, Eddie Cochran, and the Platters, captured at the precise moment their music was driving parents out of their minds.

Part jukebox musical, part sex comedy, part deranged investigation into the American entertainment industry, THE GIRL CAN'T HELP IT is a movie that understands two fundamental truths about show business: sex sells, and nobody in charge has the slightest idea what young people actually want. Tashlin makes a glorious spectacle of the whole ridiculous enterprise, somehow managing to celebrate American popular culture and accuse it of crimes against humanity at the same time.

films.title: The Gymnasts of Fisherman Colony
films.description: The birth of a gymnastics team in Pakistan provides an inspiring spark of light for a small group of girls on the margins.

films.title: The Heart of the Game
films.description:
“Sink your teeth in their necks! Draw blood!” is the rallying cry of a Seattle girls' basketball team. Imagining themselves as a pack of wolves, the girls tear into opposing teams and stand together as warriors both on and off the court. Eccentric tax professor turned high school basketball coach, Bill Resler, and star player Darnellia Russell, team up to fight the powers that would hold young women back. Narrated by Ludacris.

“Serrill's disciplined, beautifully constructed film is so propulsive, so spiritually triumphant, it's absolutely one of the best sports docs ever.” —Mike Russell, Oregonian

“There's no denying the exuberant energy and emotional force of this movie. It gets to you.” —Peter Travers, Rolling Stone

“This film should be required viewing for all teachers, coaches, and school-age kids.”
—Claudia Puig, USA Today

“An Oscar level piece of work." —Ebert & Roper

films.title: The History of Concrete
films.description: After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, filmmaker John Wilson tries to use the same formula to sell a documentary about concrete.

films.title: The Honeymoon Killers
films.description:
In the wake of BONNIE AND CLYDE, when Hollywood was busy turning murderers into glamorous countercultural heroes, Leonard Kastle set out to make a movie about criminal lovers without a trace of glamour. Based on the true story of the Lonely Hearts Killers, THE HONEYMOON KILLERS follows a pair of desperate misfits who travel the country seducing lonely widows, stealing their savings, and occasionally murdering them. Their romance unfolds in cheap boarding houses and dreary suburban interiors, photographed in grainy black-and-white that seems liable to leave ink on your fingers. Yet Kastle, an opera composer who never directed another film, scores the whole sordid enterprise to Mahler, insisting on the tragic grandeur of two people whose lives would otherwise be confined to the crime pages.

Shirley Stoler is extraordinary as Martha Beck, a lonely, furious nurse who falls hopelessly in love with professional swindler Ray Fernandez (Tony Lo Bianco) and insists on accompanying him as he romances his next victims. Stoler had always wanted to play Medea, but Hollywood had little use for a heavyset actress with ambitions toward classical tragedy. Here she finally found a role worthy of her talents, playing Martha as a woman whose longing for love has curdled into an almost infantile fury at being denied it. Posing as Ray's sister, she watches with mounting jealousy as the man she adores makes his living promising other women exactly what he's promised her. Their relationship is ridiculous, pathetic, and unmistakably passionate. The terrible joke is that Martha believes absolutely in the sincerity of a man whose only talent is lying to women.

films.title: The Joyless Economy
films.description:
Cinema can sometimes become the ground on which a person’s most intimate desires are built. Marjorie Conrad’s The Joyless Economy unfolds the inner landscape of a woman through an accumulation of film posters and images. Though it follows a woman whose relationship begins to fracture because of her film collection, the film is not ultimately about infidelity or obsession. Its deeper question concerns how two realms shape one another: a life formed under the influence of cinema, and cinema reshaped by the experience of life.

A second-person narration addressed to herself functions both as confession and as a voice of self-analysis, turning the speaker into an object of her own scrutiny. The film was made for a single viewer, yet paradoxically this private letter summons each audience member’s own memories of cinema. The films she has collected no longer remain other people’s stories. Each image encounters life, becoming a new memory and generating a new narrative.

"Exploring the long relationship between human beings and cinema known as cinephilia, The Joyless Economy becomes a small anthropology of how we collect images and invent ourselves within them." — DMZ International Documentary Festival

"A bracingly, beautifully confessional film that’s as formally inventive as it is emotionally illuminating, Marjorie Conrad’s documentary … is a daring demonstration of all that independent cinema can be." – Chase Hutchinson, The Wrap

films.title: The Kidnapping of Arabella
films.description:
Presented by Cinema Italian Style. Holly, trapped in a dead-end job, believes meeting rebellious eight-year-old Arabella is a cosmic second chance: her younger self returned. Together they embark on an unconventional road trip, discovering that two lost souls may hold the answers each has been searching for.

Following the screening: Q&A with the film's director, Carolina Cavalli, a guest of Cinema Italian Style.

films.title: The Last One for the Road
films.description: The film tells the story of Carlobianchi and Doriano, two down-on-their-luck fifty-somethings who enjoy drinking and are chasing the legend of a treasure hidden by their friend Eugenio, known as Genio, who fled to Argentina after committing fraud at the eyeglasses factory where they all worked.

films.title: The Last Temptation of Becky
films.description: Now a CIA field agent, Becky (Lulu Wilson) goes undercover in Poland to infiltrate a family running an inn at The Wolf's Lair, one of Hitler's WWII bunkers. When she learns the father, Wilhelm Reuss (Neil Patrick Harris), plans to spark the Fourth Reich, Becky must stop him.

films.title: The Leopard Man
films.description:
A black leopard escapes into the night, a small New Mexico town grows frightened, and Val Lewton and Jacques Tourneur have everything they need. Adapted from Cornell Woolrich’s Black Alibi and given its wonderfully lurid title by RKO in the wake of CAT PEOPLE, THE LEOPARD MAN turns a simple pulp premise into one of the strangest and most beautifully controlled thrillers of the 1940s—a movie built from darkness, sound, chance and the fear of being alone at exactly the wrong moment.

The final collaboration between Lewton and Tourneur keeps wandering away from the path a conventional mystery might take, following the nighttime life of the town with an almost dreamlike freedom. Ordinary errands and encounters acquire an inexplicable tension. Wind moves through empty streets. Water drips beneath a railroad trestle. Castanets click somewhere in the darkness. Tourneur and cinematographer Robert De Grasse fill the screen with pools of black so deep that simply waiting to discover what might emerge from them becomes almost unbearable, while the soundtrack makes every footstep and distant noise feel potentially significant.

At barely over an hour, THE LEOPARD MAN is lean enough to qualify as pure pulp and strange enough to continually escape its own premise. Beneath the mystery runs the fatalism of Woolrich and Lewton’s fascination with ordinary lives brushing unexpectedly against the unknown, all expressed through filmmaking of extraordinary economy and precision. Manny Farber was already championing it as one of Hollywood’s “original gems” in the early 1950s, and its nocturnal spell has only grown stronger with time. A street, a shadow, a sound in the distance: few horror films have ever needed less to make the darkness feel dangerous.

films.title: The Life We Leave
films.description:
Micah Truman has been at the forefront of shaping the market for legal human composting in Washington State. Formerly a businessman outside of the death industry, he brings on funeral directors Katey Houston and Brie Smith to workshop the humanity that is revealed when death is raw. The team paves the way in revolutionizing the future of death care by renouncing outdated funeral practices and returning to human roots of community care during the transition at the end of life. Truman creates a facility to naturalize the process, where bodies can be broken down into soil. The merger of business pitches and financial feasibility cracks open the basis of loss and grief in an extractive world to facilitate delicate and empathetic care. JJ Gerber's directorial debut accesses the transformative power of the evolving death industry at its most human.

—Aly Shwedo

“Gerber’s film makes one consider that how we leave this world may matter less than what we choose to leave behind. Is death an ending, or merely a continuation?” – Mike Ward, Should I See It

films.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
films.description: Harry Lehman is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York. Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily cancelled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie. When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.

films.title: The Parallax View
films.description: After a presidential candidate is assassinated, political reporter Joe Frady begins to suspect that the mysterious Parallax Corporation may be involved. As he investigates, others who share his suspicions start turning up dead, including his editor, Bill Rintels. Eventually, Frady uncovers a conspiracy bigger than anyone expected and must race to prevent the corporation’s next big hit as this political thriller plays out in an explosive game of cat and mouse.

films.title: The Passenger
films.description:
“What are you running away from?”
“Turn your back to the front seat.”

Lost amidst the deserts of Northern Chad, disaffected American journalist David Locke (Jack Nicholson) stumbles across the dead body of a fellow hotel acquaintance and decides to leave behind more than his sand trapped Land Rover: swapping passports, Locke abandons his identity. Renting a car “for the rest of my life” and embarking on a journey through Germany, England, and Spain, Locke soon discovers that the life he traded in for has direct connections to secret proxy wars and the international arms trade. Accompanied by a young tourist he meets in Barcelona (Maria Schneider), Locke drives further away from himself and the world while being pursued by mysterious criminals and police alike. A maestro of cinematic alienation, Michelangelo Antonioni navigates the slippery nature of identity with impeccable formal control accompanied by a career high point from Jack Nicholson.

“See the film twice and you see two films. See it a third and you see a third. So it goes.” — Robert Koehler, CinemaScope

35mm print courtesy of Sony Pictures Classics

films.title: The Promised Land
films.description: Set during the Industrial Revolution in 19th century Łódź, three entrepreneurial friends pool their resources to open a textile factory. But friendships, personal relationships and moral values are soon tested when they encounter ruthlessly competitive barons and competing self interests. An adaptation of Nobel Prize-winning author Stanisław Reymont’s novel, the film is a compelling and continually pertinent indictment of rampant capitalism and humanity’s more selfish impulses. Wajda’s first Academy Award-nominated drama remains one of his most celebrated films.

films.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
films.description:
$5 of every ticket will be donated to Seattle Pride. After getting a flat tire, two sweethearts discover the eerie mansion of a flamboyant scientist and houseful of wild characters. Through elaborate dance and rock songs, the mad scientist unveils his latest creation: a perfect, muscular man.

films.title: The Room
films.description: The unstoppable cult classic returns for it's monthly screening! Director/Writer/Producer/Leading Man Tommy Wiseau plays Johnny, a banker who likes to throw footballs with friends, mentors a drug dealing man child, loves doggies, and isn't aware that his best friend is sleeping with his future wife. Also, he did not hit her. He did naaaaaaat. Show up early for pre-show fun.

films.title: The Shining
films.description: When writer Jack Torrance (Nicholson)—who has a history of alcoholism and child abuse—takes a job as winter caretaker for a hotel high in the Rocky Mountains, he, his wife (Duvall) and their psychic young son will be isolated until spring. But once the first blizzard closes the road out, the accumulated power of evil deeds committed at the hotel begins to drive Jack mad. Now there may be no escape for his wife and son in this haunting madness, memory and family violence.

films.title: The Store
films.description:
THE STORE is a film about the main Neiman-Marcus store and corporate headquarters in Dallas. The sequences in the film include the selection, presentation, marketing, pricing, advertising and selling of a vast array of consumer products including designer clothes and furs, jewelry, perfumes, shoes, electronic products, sportswear, china and porcelain and many other goods. The internal management and organizational aspects of a large corporation are shown, i.e., sales meetings, development of marketing and advertising strategies, training, personnel practices and sales techniques.

“…witnessing how an establishment deftly caters to such appetites makes for an engrossing spectacle… Only Wiseman seems able to consistently capture those tiny, illuminating surprises that stay with us long after he’s through with us.” –Harry F. Waters, Newsweek

films.title: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers
films.description:
Barbara Stanwyck has everything a woman could want: a business empire, a powerful husband, and a murder nobody knows she committed. In THE STRANGE LOVE OF MARTHA IVERS, she rules a Pennsylvania factory town alongside her husband (Kirk Douglas, in his debut), an alcoholic district attorney whose political authority is inversely proportional to his authority at home. Seventeen years after a childhood crime brought them together, the unexpected return of an old sweetheart (Van Heflin) sends their miserable marriage into a fresh crisis. Meanwhile, Lizabeth Scott plays an ex-con who has the bad luck to wander into a town where the respectable citizens are considerably more dangerous than the criminals.

Directed by Lewis Milestone from a screenplay by Robert Rossen, this wonderfully bitter combination of film noir and Gothic melodrama is as much about the corruptions of wealth and power as it is about the terrible things people do for love. Stanwyck is magnificent as a woman who has acquired everything except the ability to enjoy it, while Douglas plays a man who can intimidate an entire town but can't stand up to his own wife. Neither seems quite sure whether they hate each other more than they hate themselves. With its magnificent shadows, feverish performances, and almost operatic emotional cruelty, this is Hollywood melodrama at its most gloriously unhappy.

films.title: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre Part 2
films.description:
This movie serves up everything one could want from a Thanksgiving movie, including a climatic family dinner scene, and Baron von Terror looks forward to sharing this fright-feast with you!

Leatherface meats a nice radio DJ and invites her to family dinner. Dennis Hopper shows up, too. Good times!

You do not need to see the first one to follw the plot.

For real, though, Texas 2 has earned a solid reputation over the years for taking a much more comedic tone to the mayhem, with a truly unique script that still feels fresh and twisted to this day. The Baron can't wait to unpack it with you. plus he's giving away prizes! Woooooooo!

films.title: The VelociPastor and The VelociPastor 2 (double feature)
films.description:
A double feature of dino-namic proportions!

The epic saga of Doug Jones (Gregory James Cohan), a priest who travels to China after losing his parents and inherits a mysterious ability that allows him to turn into a dinosaur. In the first VELOCIPASTOR, Doug—with the help of a Lady of the Night, Carol (Alyssa Kempinski)—harnesses his newfound power to fight crime. And ninjas.

Then, in the brand new follow-up, THE VELOCIPASTOR 2, Doug and Carol travel to the port city of Milan, where they have to solve a series of murders committed by a sex-maniac killer at an Italian Fertility Festival. And Soviet Spies. Oh, and INTERPOL’s there, too.

Please note: There will be a 10-minute intermission between features.

films.title: The Wedding
films.description: An intellectual poet and peasant woman unite in matrimony, with their wedding party attended by a class-crossing assortment of society. However, the veneer of harmony is broken when ghosts – drawn from local history and legend – appear out of the fog to the revellers. Wajda’s psychedelic adaptation of Stanisław Wyspiański’s influential 1901 play where (as stated in the prologue) “everything in [the] story is true —even the dreams,” employs dizzying cinematography and creates an eerie atmosphere to offer a searing critique of the nation’s phantoms. It became one of the most culturally significant works of Polish cinema.

films.title: The Witch
films.description:
New England, 1630. Upon threat of banishment by the church, an English farmer leaves his colonial plantation, relocating his wife and five children to a remote plot of land on the edge of an ominous forest—within which lurks an unknown evil. Strange and unsettling things begin to happen almost immediately—animals turn malevolent, crops fail, and one child disappears as another becomes seemingly possessed by an evil spirit. With suspicion and paranoia mounting, family members accuse teenage daughter Thomasin of witchcraft, charges she adamantly denies. As circumstances grow more treacherous, each family member’s faith, loyalty and love become tested in shocking and unforgettable ways.

In this exquisitely made and terrifying new horror film, the age-old concepts of witchcraft, black magic and possession are innovatively brought together to tell the intimate and riveting story of one family’s frightful unraveling in the New England wilderness.

films.title: Tokyo Story
films.description: A profoundly stirring evocation of elemental humanity and universal heartbreak, Tokyo Story is the crowning achievement of the unparalleled Yasujiro Ozu. The film, which follows an aging couple’s journey to visit their grown children in bustling postwar Tokyo, surveys the rich and complex world of family life with the director’s customary delicacy and incisive perspective on social mores. Featuring lovely performances from Ozu regulars Chishu Ryu and Setsuko Hara, Tokyo Story plumbs and deepens the director’s recurring theme of generational conflict, creating what is without question one of cinema’s mightiest masterpieces.

films.title: Totally 80's Sing Along
films.description: Bust out your leg warmers and skinny ties! The TOTALLY 80'S SING ALONG returns to Central Cinema featuring favorite videos from the dawn of MTV and beyond. Prince, Madonna, Wham, Cyndi Lauper and tons more await! All subtitled for your sing along enjoyment. RADICOOL!

films.title: True Stories
films.description:
Music maestro David Byrne took inspiration from tabloid headlines to create the only film he's directed, an ode to the extraordinariness of ordinary American life. Byrne is also our on screen host, a visitor to the town of Virgil, Texas, who introduces us to the locals as they prepare for the town's 150th anniversary and the Celebration of Specialness. We meet a local singer who just wants to find his true love, a woman who can't seem to ever get out of bed, and a community leader who really enjoys veggies.

Using Talking Heads music to stich together the town's happenings, Byrne creates a loving tapestry of stories, showing his audience that everyday life always has interesting tales beneath the simple surface.

films.title: Two-Lane Blacktop
films.description:
An unnamed drag racing duo (James Taylor and "The Beach Boys"' Dennis Wilson, referred to as The Driver and Mechanic in novelist Rudy Wurlitzer’s screenplay) head eastward from Los Angeles in their souped up ‘55 Chevy. They cross paths with an orbit-orange GTO and its wandering loner of a driver played by Warren Oates, bedecked throughout in a kaleidoscope wardrobe of cashmere sweaters. Vying for the attention of a restless hitchhiker in tow (Laurie Bird), the trio embark on a race for pink slips across six southern states. Filmed in sequence and entirely on location, Monte Hellman’s low budget masterpiece of highway philosophy features gorgeous widescreen photography and sparse, existential dialogue that captures a moment in time when, as Vincent Canby states, “faith in God is a lot less important, less immediate and even less mystical than faith in the internal combustion engine.” The quintessential American road film.

“In Two-Lane Blacktop [the road] becomes something altogether different and far more interesting: a repository of dreams and fantasies, for squares, hipsters, and obsessives alike…It is a movie about loneliness, and the attempts made by people to connect with one another and maintain their solitude at the same time—an impossible task, an elusive dream.” — Kent Jones

35mm print courtesy of Universal

films.title: Vagabond
films.description: Sandrine Bonnaire won the Best Actress César for her portrayal of the defiant young drifter Mona, found frozen to death in a ditch at the beginning of Vagabond. Agnès Varda pieces together Mona’s story through flashbacks told by those who encountered her (played by a largely nonprofessional cast), producing a splintered portrait of an enigmatic woman. With its sparse, poetic imagery, Vagabond is a stunner, and won Varda the top prize at the Venice Film Festival.

films.title: VHS Über Alles Presents…
films.description:
Experience cult movies in analog glory! Seattle’s ultimate VHS screening series delivers an unstoppable onslaught of 0.5-inch magnetic power. All we can tell you about the film is this:

It's a special Friday the 13th show featuring: MADNESS! MURDER! MAYHEM!

Just $5 gets you a seat before we hit “play” on the all-powerful VCR.

films.title: Whalefall
films.description: Following the death of his father (Josh Brolin), Jay Gardiner (Austin Abrams) goes diving off the central Coast of California in search of his remains, but is swallowed by a massive sperm whale. While trapped inside its belly with only one hour of oxygen left, Jay comes to realize that the hard-earned lessons his father imparted may be the key to his escape.

films.title: Where Is the Fiesta?
films.description: Set in contemporary Rome, Where Is the Fiesta? follows Leo and Irene, a couple in their mid-thirties who, after three and a half months together, still have no idea where their relationship is heading. With New Year’s Eve just ten days away, they must decide whether to spend it together and take the next step toward making their relationship official. Leo is an aspiring actor from Fucecchio who juggles a string of odd jobs to make ends meet, while Irene is a screenwriter and screenwriting teacher torn between her feelings and her doubts about their future.

films.title: Wicker
films.description: An audacious comedic fable about sex, marriage, and the absurdities of social convention, Wicker tells the wholly original love story of an ostracized fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) who commissions a husband to be made by the local basketmaker (Peter Dinklage). When her wicker husband (Alexander Skarsgård) proves more spectacular than she ever imagined, his soulful spirit and unique prowess awaken something inside her, setting off a wave of jealousy, fascination, and upheaval that threatens the very fabric of village life.

films.title: Wild Boys of the Road
films.description:
“Police Alarmed at Increase of Wild Boys of the Road: Seek Solution to Problem of Homeless Waifs”

Faced with the realization that their middle-class folks do not have enough money to feed them, buddies Tommy and Edie decide that the best course to alleviate that burden is to do what an estimated 250,000 other American teens did during the height of the Great Depression: live on the road and criss-cross the country on freight trains. Riding the rails from city to city through the Midwest to the east coast, the pair have their newfound sense of freedom challenged as they face the desperation, poverty and exploitation lost orphans experience in the slums. Despite the ever present railway detectives, the wild boys find solidarity amongst each other and turn a hobo camp into a mini society. In many respects the archetypal filmmaker of the pre-Code era, “Wild Bill” Wellmann’s features in the early ‘30s packed a gritty punch of hard edged social realism, an unflinching look at the traumas of the era.

35mm print courtesy of the Library of Congress

films.title: Wild Horse Nine
films.description: Two CIA agents (John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell) are sent on a mission to Easter Island, where one faces an existential crisis over his past actions, in Martin McDonagh’s latest dark comedy.

films.title: Wildwood
films.description: After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness—an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover the strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. From Oscar®-nominated and BAFTA®-winning LAIKA, Wildwood is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice, and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar.

films.title: Will Success Spoil Rock Hunter?
films.description:
What if everything wrong with America could be traced back to advertising? And what if the only way to save yourself was to become the most famous man in the country? Frank Tashlin tackles these important questions in WILL SUCCESS SPOIL ROCK HUNTER?, a candy-colored nervous breakdown about sex, celebrity, capitalism, and the terrible things people will do to get a key to the executive bathroom. Tony Randall plays Rock Hunter, a lowly advertising executive whose career depends on convincing Hollywood bombshell Rita Marlowe (Jayne Mansfield) to endorse a brand of lipstick. When Rita recruits him to pose as her boyfriend, Rock becomes an overnight national sex symbol, an achievement that comes as a considerable surprise to everyone who has ever met him.

Having already exposed the dangers of comic books and rock and roll, Tashlin now turns his attention to the people responsible for selling them to us. The result is a merciless CinemaScope assault on Madison Avenue, Hollywood, television, celebrity worship, and the American conviction that happiness can be achieved with the correct combination of consumer products. Mansfield brilliantly parodies her own bombshell persona, Randall gradually loses his mind, and an entire nation seems willing to surrender its dignity in exchange for a little publicity. Along the way, Tashlin interrupts his own movie to make fun of television, stages a series of commercials for products that might actually kill you, and reveals the executive bathroom as the spiritual center of American capitalism. It's one of the funniest movies ever made about selling your soul and discovering that nobody's particularly interested in buying it.

films.title: Withdrawal
films.description:
Writer/director/editor Aaron Strand scheduled to join for an in-person intro and Q&A. Raw, unflinching, and surprisingly funny, WITHDRAWAL was shot on miniDV in Athens, GA for a budget of $60k and is a prime example of indie filmmaking at its finest.

Artistic lovers Viv (Millie Rose Evans) and Jay (Brent Michal) are trapped in a vicious cycle of codependent heroin addiction. When Viv's wealthy parents hire an interventionist to take her to rehab, the couple decides to go it alone with nothing but a suboxone prescription and each other. All they have to do is survive one harrowing night of withdrawal. As the hours tick by, physical, mental, and emotional torments send them searching through fractured memories, trying to figure out where it all went wrong.

Winner of a dozen awards on the festival circuit, including Best Feature/Best Director at the Art of Brooklyn Film Festival and Best Actress at the Kanazawa Film Festival.

Local Seattle filmmaker Matt Dy’s short “We’re All in This Together” will precede the feature.

films.title: Wto/99
films.description:
From November 30th to December 3rd 1999, tens of thousands of people occupied the streets of downtown Seattle to make known their concerns about the existence of the World Trade Organization and its impacts on the environment, human rights, and labor in the largest protests against economic globalization the US has ever seen.

The protests brought together people from divergent sections of society—anarchists, environmentalists, labor unions, consumer protection advocates, pro-democracy groups, and even religious organizations.

These protestors gathered in direct action hoping to dissuade world leadership from continued support of the WTO and strived to focus the public’s attention to the kind of future the WTO would bring forth.

Building from a thousand-hour archive, which includes more than 400 hours of never-before-seen footage, WTO’99 reanimates the ideological conflicts that drew thousands to the streets of Seattle in hopes for a better future. The film is an immersive visual artifact of a week that brought 40,000 people together to warn of environmental collapse, the vanishing middle class, and what the full inclusion of China in the World Trade Organization would mean for our collective future. The protesters—seen as a rabble-rousing nuisance at the time, yet appearing prophetic today—were met with extreme violence by a militarized police force, an all-too-fitting way to usher in a new century; one that is now defined by US failure to address climate change and increasing state aggression.

films.title: You Can See Everything
films.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything.

films.title: You Sorta Know It's Gonna End
films.description:
From staples of the independent Canadian scene, filmmakers Kalil Haddad and Ryan Steel present their new shorts cycle You Sorta Know It’s Gonna End. Conceived as a video mixtape, this hour-long compendium echoes the era of VHS rips, featuring ten classic shorts from both directors, alongside the new collaboration ‘BAND PRACTICE’.

A bold new voice in queer experimental film, Kalil Haddad’s global tour of his previous collection ‘He Never Dies : The Films of Kalil Haddad’ established him as a provocateur; reckoning with a fraught visual aesthetic which inhabits the burning edge of cultural danger and morality. He recently starred in Isiah Medina’s 2025 debut feature, Gangsterism (2025).

Ryan Steel is a member of the Winnipeg Film Group, previously working with established voices of the Canadian avant-garde such as directors Guy Maddin (My Winnipeg, Rumours) and Grace Glowiki (Dead Lover). He brings to this work his notion of material, analog and DIY aesthetic – together, crafting You Sorta Know It’s Gonna End as a tangle of nostalgia, masculine crisis and caustic youth.

films.title: Young Frankenstein
films.description: Following in the footsteps of his infamous grandfather, Dr. Frederick Frankenstein inherits his ancestor's Transylvanian castle and laboratory. He initially attempts to distance himself from the family's legacy, but is drawn into recreating the experiments that brought his grandfather's monster to life. With the help of Igor, the bubbly Inga, and the unsettling Frau Blücher, Frederick’s plans are complicated by a living monster and the unexpected arrival of his fiancée, Elizabeth, leading to chaotic and hilarious consequences.

films.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
films.description: Latif, a devoutly religious hitman, struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him – and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

films.title: Zero Patience
films.description:
To commemorate World AIDS Day 2026, Northwest Film Forum is excited to present John Greyson’s movie musical Zero Patience. Unconventional (and fun!) in form and incredibly imaginative in its premise, Zero Patience is a film that confronts historical bigotry and damaging myths that surround the mysterious (and patently fictional) “Patient Zero” while also remaining campy, educational, and ambitious.

Screens with Song From An Angel (David Weissman, United States, 1988, 5min)

Made two weeks before his death from AIDS, Song From An Angel features San Franciscan performer Rodney Price as he tap dances and sings an incredibly dark, yet endearingly funny, song about his own death: “I’ve Got Less Time Than You.”

films.title: Zi
films.description:
In Hong Kong, a young woman haunted by visions of her future self meets a stranger who changes the course of her night—and possibly her life. Kogonada plays with — and returns to — form in this sensitive cinematic poem. Held within a stylish jaunt through the streets of Hong Kong, zi is a film with soul and a wavelike confidence that commits to recursivity as a mode and central theme. Kogonada regulars Michelle Mao, Haley Lu Richardson, and Jin Ha carefully portray transitory misfits, grappling with a clever fusion of existential anxiety, romantic misgiving, and personal memory. Somewhere between sci-fi and supernatural, a deep, easy warmth takes root. Kogonada crafts a decidedly contained film, exploring a pervasive sense of unmooring, yet cultivating an unrelenting sense of peace. Through the igniting/smoldering embers of relationships lost/forming, zi is an invitation to surrender to Kogonada’s truly indie world of temporal fragmentation.

“An instant classic.”

— Richard Brody, The New Yorker

“Bold, beautiful, and beguiling. Michelle Mao crafts what ought to be a breakout performance for the ages.”

— Chase Hutchinson, TheWrap
